| absolute-path-from-one-machine | A script that names one machine's absolute path (a drive letter, a user folder, a checkout location) as its only location for the repo, a secrets file or a data folder works only on that machine; on a second machine it fails, or worse, silently reads or writes somewhere else. | accepted-decision-without-owning-row | A decision row that CHANGES existing behaviour (a SPEC CHANGE) is accepted and cited by requirements, but no builder-sequence row or work item names the code change it needs, so the code keeps the old behaviour indefinitely while the spec says otherwise. It is a data-availability limit after hours, not a defect of the target path: in market hours the same strategies answer. | unguarded | scope, spec_ref |

| basket-tag-exceeds-publisher-limit | Any identifier built for one channel from the limit of a different channel of the same vendor (the API order tag allows 20 characters, the Publisher basket page allows 8) exceeds the stricter channel's limit once a counter inside it grows a digit, so the feature works for the first nine entities and fails for every one after. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |

| brief-rule-from-memory | Any product rule an orchestrator writes into a builder brief from memory or paraphrase, instead of quoting the spec text it rests on, can be wrong, and the builder then implements the wrong rule faithfully and its tests lock it in, costing a full fix round when a verifier catches it. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| broker-reply-shape-unproven-at-domain-boundary | Domain code built and verified only against fakes that already hold the domain's own types (Decimal money, contract keys, aware times) can be fully correct and still unusable: the first real broker reply is refused at the boundary, because nothing converts the broker's real shape (JSON numbers, SDK floats, recorder strings, a flat row with a zero average price, a symbol string instead of the contract key, naive local times) into those types. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |

| ci-apt-mirror-stall | A CI step that installs system packages with apt on a hosted runner can spend its whole timeout on one stalled mirror download, because apt's default per-request timeout is long and it retries the same slow fetch; the job fails red with no code defect, and a re-run is the only recovery unless apt is told to fail over fast. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| ci-path-filter-misses-dependency-change | A CI workflow limited by a path filter to the files of one layer never runs when a change lands only in a layer that layer imports; the dependency change breaks its tests on main with no red check anywhere, and every later PR that does touch the filtered paths inherits failures it did not cause. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| client-message-resets-rate-limit | A per-stream rate limit that is reset whenever the client sends a message lets any client bypass it by re-sending, turning a server-paced push into client-driven work. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| closed-market-label-time-from-frame | A market-closed label states a price time taken from a field that records when a frame ARRIVED (or when the broker stamped a post-close packet) instead of when the price was made; outside market hours every price was made at the close of its session, so any label built from arrival or packet time tells the user a false time (e.g. 'Prices are from 28 Oct 07:46' for the 27 Oct close). | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| closed-market-rule-per-surface | Any screen or answer that shows market data after hours, where the closed-market rule (ADR-177 one banner, ADR-200 (2) no stale/read-time labels, ADR-197/ADR-212 numbers from the last close) is applied by that surface's own code instead of one shared path: each surface that was not touched keeps showing 'stale since <read time>', per-cell stale sentences, a 'live' tag, the fetch time as the price time, or blank numbers. | unguarded | scope, spec_ref |
| daily-list-trims-far-strikes-trips-truncation-guard | A truncation guard on a reference-data reload that judges a shrunk list by a percentage (of the index, or of one expiry) refuses a legitimate daily trim of far-from-the-money members, because the source drops only the far end of every expiry at once; the refused reload leaves the catalogue not same-day and a downstream gate then refuses every action that needs a same-day list. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| daily-load-misses-intraday-additions | Any reference-data load that runs once a day assumes the source list is fixed for the day; when the source adds members during the day (new strikes, new contracts), everything listed after the load is missing from the catalogue until the next day, and anything keyed on it (subscriptions, strategies, validations) refuses or ignores those members. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| date-stamp-typed-from-memory | Any date or time written into a status document, decision row or file name from the author's sense of 'today' instead of the system clock drifts; a long session that crosses midnight, or one that plans for 'tomorrow morning', stamps the future, and every reader then trusts a date that did not happen yet. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| db-role-connection-limit-below-pool-size | A database role whose connection limit is smaller than the maximum a single application process's pool can open (plus any second process sharing the role) fails under load with 'too many connections' that surfaces as a 500 on whichever request needs a connection next, intermittently and only when several requests overlap. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| db-role-limit-below-pool-size | A database role whose connection limit is smaller than what the processes using it may open (any one process's pool size plus overflow, summed over every process on the role): whenever load grows a pool past the limit - a page that fans out one request per row, a second app process, a test run - the database refuses new connections to every process on that role, including ones doing unrelated, critical work. Wider shape: a shared hard cap that no process sizes itself against is exhausted by whichever process bursts first. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| db-tests-outside-the-row-red-only-in-ci | A change to a migration, a database function or a route's reply breaks database-backed tests in OTHER files (round-trip, pin and exact-reply tests written when an older state was newest), and nothing local runs them: the gate runs only the database-free app tests, and the builder runs only its own files, so the red appears only in CI after the push. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| dependent-tests-not-run-stale-later | A change to a shared module (a route helper, a socket constructor, a freshness rule) is verified by running only the tests its own work item names; a test elsewhere that imports or fakes the changed code keeps asserting the old behaviour, stays red on the branch, and surfaces rows or days later in someone else's verification (or in CI at the end), where its cause is no longer obvious. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| design-misses-cross-cutting-safeguard | A design written from the requirement it implements (and the ADRs that requirement cites) misses a safeguard defined in a cross-cutting decision that applies to it only by reference from a third document; the design then contradicts a standing decision without labelling it a SPEC CHANGE, and only an adversarial review finds it. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| docs-only-pr-skips-record-scans | A pull request that changes only records (evidence, work items, findings, decisions) is classed docs-only and runs no test suite, but some repo tests read exactly those records (reach check over evidence, tests_required over work items, spec integrity); such a PR merges green and the first full run - the push to main - goes red, blocking every open pull request. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| domain-test-imports-app-package | A test in the domain suite (`tests/`, standard library + domain package only) that imports the application package runs the application's import-time side effects - here the W-024 root log redaction - inside the shared test process, so later, unrelated tests in the same run see altered global state (log records without exc_info) and fail only in the combined order CI uses, never when run alone. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| duplicate-acceptance-criterion-id | Any requirement file can carry two acceptance criteria with the same AC id and still pass the project's lint, so tests, evidence files and citations that name that id become ambiguous. | guarded | scope, spec_ref |

| e2e-stand-in-drifts-from-server | A Playwright spec that replaces a server route or socket with a hand-written stand-in keeps the server's OLD behaviour when the server changes (a new protocol field, an edit the route now applies); the page, written against the new server, then never reaches the state the spec waits for, and the only catch is the Playwright CI job after the push. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| engine-input-chosen-per-caller | When each caller of an engine function chooses the input it passes (which price an IV is solved from, which time, which spot), two screens show two different engine numbers for the same thing at the same instant; each caller's own tests pass because none compares the callers with each other. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| fallback-time-claims-missing-data | A 'last updated <time>' label that falls back to the current time when no data was ever received tells the user data arrived when none did; the honest label for never-received data is a different message, not a time. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| fill-not-exactly-once | Any path by which a broker fill changes order or position state that is not exactly-once, keyed by broker identity, and validated against the exact order it claims to fill. | first-live-frame-before-first-price | A live socket that computes and pushes its first frame the moment it connects, before every contract it needs has had its first tick, reports a failure state (here REFUSED: a derived input such as the forward cannot be computed yet) instead of a waiting state; the screen flashes an error on every open and every reconnect, and the error clears by itself one tick later. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| fixture-retag-by-string-breaks-on-format-change | Any test that adapts recorded real-world data to its own fixture ids by string surgery on a product-built identifier (an order tag, a key, a code) re-implements the product's builder; when the builder's format changes, every such test on every branch built before the change breaks at once, and each branch's CI finds it separately. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| fixture-symbol-not-in-catalogue | Any test fixture that types a broker tradingsymbol (or a symbol/expiry pair) from memory instead of taking it from the real instrument catalogue can pass for months while encoding a contract Zerodha does not list; the defect surfaces only when some later code checks the catalogue, and every test built on the fixture then has to change. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| freshness-judged-on-request-start-clock | Any live-data freshness rule that compares a feed timestamp against a 'now' read at the START of a request, before slow reads (broker margin, positions) that run while the feed keeps ticking, refuses every tick newer than that 'now' (a rule of 0 <= now - t fails for t after now), so a healthy, fast feed reads as out of date exactly when the data is freshest. | gate-output-read-by-eye | A gate whose failing output has no final verdict line (only per-item lines, some good, some bad) gets reported as passing by an agent that reads the output by eye instead of its exit code; the report is then relayed as evidence. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| gate-run-in-parallel-with-its-action | A check and the action it is meant to gate (push, merge, deploy) issued as separate parallel tool calls: the action does not wait for the check, so a failing check gates nothing; a same-command chain guard (gate_before_commit) cannot see across calls. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| gate-run-several-times-per-commit | The same full local gate runs more than once on the same commit (builder, orchestrator, then --pre-push), each taking minutes, and CI then re-runs everything again; the repeats add time and extra chances for a load-related false red without adding evidence. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| gate-timed-test-flakes-under-load | A local check that runs an external tool under a fixed wall-clock limit and treats a timeout as an empty (clean) result turns into a false failure when the machine is loaded by parallel agents: the assertion expects output, the tool is killed at the limit, and the gate stops on a red that has nothing to do with the change. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| generic-plan-under-stale-statistics | A prepared statement reused by an async PostgreSQL driver switches to the server's cached generic plan after a few executions; if the table's statistics are wrong at that moment (e.g. captured as 0 rows by an ANALYZE that ran during an uncommitted bulk load), the generic plan can be catastrophically slow and every later execution times out, while the first executions looked merely slow. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| guard-as-forbidden-list | Any guard - a database CHECK, a type check, a wording check, a privilege check, or a test that is meant to detect a reopened hole - written as a list of FORBIDDEN things (named bad shapes, named bad types, bad words, bad privilege paths) lets through everything its author did not imagine; the guard must state what IS allowed (exact key sets, a closed type per slot, a closed name list) and refuse the rest, and its test must enumerate the allowed shape against every other type, generated rather than hand-listed. This is the wider shape of privilege-guard-as-denylist, advice-wording-denylist-per-module, secret-filter-by-key-name and jsonpath-check-lax-mode-unwraps-arrays. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| guard-by-banned-shapes | A guard that lists the forbidden WAYS of doing something (banned characters in a value, banned code shapes or spellings in a source scan, banned constructors) is never complete when the language or format offers open-ended ways to reach the same result; each review round finds the next unlisted way. A guard is complete only when it mints the value itself from a typed source and re-mints and compares at the point of use, or when it is an allow-list over a small CLOSED set (the characters a path may hold; the files allowed to use each reflection entry point). | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| guard-without-killing-test | Any safety guard (an if-refuse/block/raise that protects money or state) with no test that fails when the guard is removed can be deleted or weakened in a later change with the suite still green; the guard's protection then depends on nobody touching that line. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| health-dropped-at-response-boundary | A value that carries its own data health inside the domain (a forward from a stale spot, a level from a delayed quote) loses that health when it is turned into the API response, so the screen shows a number built from stale data as if it were current - often next to other values that do say stale. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| held-without-platform-fill-invisible-to-ledger | A position that enters a strategy without a platform fill (adopted from the broker, moved in, restored) is invisible to every check that derives 'what the platform holds' from its own fill ledger: the send guard sees room to buy it again, the exit sees nothing to close, and once the broker row disappears the ledger (0) agrees with the broker (0), so the gap reads as a 'missing leg' instead of a mismatch. | identifier-unique-only-by-convention | An identifier that people or logs read (an error code, a tag, a numbered row) whose uniqueness is kept only by each author picking the next free number by hand collides as soon as two parallel branches pick at the same time or one author misses an existing use; the collision is invisible unless a test asserts uniqueness over the generated set, and checking a DIFFERENT key for uniqueness (the template id) gives false comfort. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| instrument-identity-keyed-on-one-broker | Any instrument store whose identity is one broker's own token or trading symbol cannot hold the same contract's identifiers from another broker, and every table, cache and subscription that joins on that broker id has to be re-keyed when a second broker arrives; the identifier the exchange itself assigns is the one every broker shares. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| interpolated-level-finer-than-paise-refused | Any level the engine derives by interpolation or by subtracting a flat amount (a breakeven after charges, a zero crossing between two strikes) can carry more decimal places than paise; a downstream function that validates its input as a money value (at most 2 decimals) then refuses it and the whole figure fails. | jsonpath-check-lax-mode-unwraps-arrays | A database CHECK written as JSON-path filters over a free JSONB document refuses only the shapes its author listed: PostgreSQL's default lax mode unwraps an array wherever the path expects a scalar, so a value wrapped in an array (or an empty array) satisfies every per-value test, and a position whose value is only type-checked accepts any text of that type. | keepalive-counted-as-live-data | A liveness or health state that is refreshed by ANY inbound traffic on a connection (heartbeats, pings, keep-alive bytes) reports the data stream as live after the data itself has stopped; the connection is alive, the data is not, and the screen shows Connected indefinitely. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| last-live-answer-kept-after-drop | A browser view that renders numbers from the last answer it holds keeps showing that answer's numbers after ITS OWN live connection drops, until a later answer replaces it: when the fallback read is slow, hangs, fails, or an older read resolves after the drop, an old number stays on screen looking live. Wider shape: liveness must be a property of the moment the number is shown (the view's own connection now), never of the answer object that happened to arrive last. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| live-read-without-own-subscription | A request needs a live value (an index level, a futures price) from a shared streaming feed but never subscribes that value itself: it reads whatever the feed currently holds, so it works only while some other screen or socket happens to hold the same instrument, and fails for the user who opens that feature on its own. | live-work-shares-test-database | Running the app live against the same database the test suites use leaves committed rows (a real catalogue, a saved draft, a broker session) that tests written for an empty database then trip over, so local database tests fail for an environmental reason and verifiers must discount failures by hand. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| liveness-from-a-file-nobody-deletes | A check that decides 'is X running right now?' from the presence of a marker file is wrong whenever the writer does not reliably delete the marker: it reports X running long after X ended, and every block or wait built on it stalls for the full staleness window. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| liveness-from-shared-subscribers | A per-client 'is my data live?' answer computed from a shared resource's state (any subscriber on the shared fan-out) instead of the asking client's own connection: whenever another client holds the same inputs, a client whose own connection dropped is told its data is live, so its screen shows numbers without the not-live label. | local-ci-mirror-runs-a-subset | A local 'mirror' of CI that runs only some of CI's steps reports green while CI is red on a step it skips, so a push or merge attempt that relied on it costs a CI round; the mirror must be generated from, or checked against, the CI workflow's own step list rather than maintained by hand. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| local-gate-step-argv-over-8k-windows | A local gate that rewrites a CI step (appending the chosen test files to every test call) and hands the whole multi-line script to the shell as ONE command-line argument breaks once the script passes ~8 KB on Windows Git bash: the script is cut, the shell reports a syntax error, and no test runs. | money-parsed-through-float | Any adapter that reads a JSON reply with the default number parser turns every price, margin and charge into a binary float before it becomes a Decimal, so values like 291444.67000000004 enter the money path and rupee totals pick up representation error. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| money-value-computed-outside-engine | Any money value (premium, P&L, value) that a consumer module re-computes from leg prices instead of reading it from the one calculation engine can silently drop a factor the engine applies (quantity, sign, instrument kind), so the consumer and the engine disagree. | guarded | scope, spec_ref |
| net-only-read-misses-roundtrip | Any reconciliation that decides what happened from an end-of-period NET quantity alone treats every round trip inside that period (buy then sell of the same contract, or the reverse) as 'nothing happened': the trades, their fills and their P&L vanish. Wider shape: a summary number cannot prove the absence of the events it sums. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| new-answer-state-without-reader-sweep | A change that adds a new value to a state field the server sends (a new answer state, kind or status) is checked on the server only; every client reader written for the old set of values silently drops or mis-draws the new one, and nothing fails until an end-to-end test of a screen happens to reach that state. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| normalise-before-validate | Any input normaliser that changes the text (upper/lower/casefold, strip/trim, Unicode folding) before checking it against a strict pattern can turn a malformed value into a different, valid-looking value, so a bad row is silently repaired into someone else's identifier instead of being reported. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| orchestrator-context-over-limit | A long-running orchestrator session keeps growing its context past the 250k-token limit set by ADR-178, so every later turn re-sends a huge context and the orchestrator alone burns about half of the session's tokens. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| outcome-multi-expiry-unhandled-500 | A domain function that raises a typed exception for an input shape the user can legitimately build (legs on two expiries) with no route-level mapping to a catalogue user-facing error returns a bare HTTP 500 instead of a message the user can act on. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| overlap-gate-refuses-generated-files | A dispatch-time overlap gate that compares the files two rows touch counts generated or shared registry files as overlap, so two rows with no real product overlap are serialised and the second sits idle. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| own-figure-labelled-as-broker-figure | A figure the platform derives from the broker's answer (the broker's number plus a platform rule) is shown under the broker's name, so the user reads our number as the broker's authority. Wider shape: once a value is adjusted, every label that names its source must change with it; a field named after its origin ('Zerodha says') outlives the rule that changed its meaning. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| owner-question-blocks-dispatchable-work | The orchestrator asks the owner a question with the interactive tool while independent work is ready to dispatch: the tool stops the orchestrator until the owner answers, so ready briefs wait for the whole answer time. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| paper-plan-diverges-from-position | Any screen or figure that reads a paper-tracked strategy's saved plan (its latest revision and planned entry prices) instead of the legs and prices actually recorded for the paper position, once the plan has been saved again or the fills differ from the plan. | guarded | scope, spec_ref |
| parallel-branches-green-alone-red-together | Two work items built in parallel branches each pass CI on their own base, but one adds a repo-wide guard (an import scan, an inventory, an allowlist) that the other's new code violates; the clash shows only when the branches meet, so a branch merged first can turn the other red after it was verified. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| pipe-masks-gate-exit-code | A failing step does not stop the step after it: a gate piped into a filter (`gate \| tail`) takes the filter's exit status, and a command on its own line (or after `;`) runs whatever the line before returned - so a following commit, push or merge goes ahead after a failed gate; chaining with && is not enough when the gate's output is piped. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| positions-reply-refused-for-non-platform-rows | A reader that must resolve every row of a broker reply against the platform's own catalogue refuses the WHOLE reply when the account holds any row the platform can never own (a stock, another underlying, another exchange), so a fail-closed gate downstream blocks every action for every strategy - the user's unrelated activity disables the product. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| pr-exceeds-merge-gate-file-limit | A process that batches work into one pull request (a chunk, an integration branch) can outgrow a merge gate that reads the PR's file list from an API with a fixed cap; the gate then refuses the PR at the very end, after every review and CI run, and no history split may exist that brings each part under the cap. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| pr-text-closes-issue-unintended | A code host that closes issues from free text (GitHub: a closing keyword - close/fix/resolve and their forms, optional colon - directly before #N in a PR body or in a commit message reaching the default branch) closes a whole issue whenever an author writes a qualified reference ('Fix #263 items 1-3') or ordinary prose ('the clash with #275 is resolved: #275 moved'); without a check on the text, every partial fix and every prose mention is a possible wrong close, found only later from the issue list. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| pre-existing-failure-claim-not-checked-on-base | Any claim that a failing test is 'pre-existing' or 'unrelated' that is not proven by running it on a clean checkout of the base branch can hide a regression the change itself caused, and turns it into a deferred issue nobody fixes. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| prefilter-narrower-than-parser | A cheap pre-filter placed in front of a parser (skip rows whose exchange, type or kind is not in a short list) silently drops rows the parser itself was later taught to accept. The parser's tests pass, the caller's tests pass on data without those rows, and the loss shows only when the dropped rows are needed downstream. The accept rule must live in one place: the pre-filter asks the parser's own accept test, or there is no pre-filter. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| privilege-guard-as-denylist | Any guard that protects data by refusing a list of forbidden privilege paths (superuser, a named role membership, table ownership) misses every path not on the list, because a database grants power through many routes (database ownership, schema ownership, role membership, default PUBLIC grants); the guard must instead assert that the role's effective privileges are exactly an allowed set. Wider shape of secret-filter-by-key-name: a denylist over an open-ended space is never complete. | guarded | scope, spec_ref |
| process-change-narrows-safety-rule | A recommendation to change the delivery process (review tiers, round caps, verifier timing, guard scope) narrows an existing safety rule without saying so, and the owner approves it before any independent review; past real catches would then reach main. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| process-kill-by-name-hits-others | An agent stops its own stale process by NAME (`taskkill /IM python.exe`, `Stop-Process -Name python`, `pkill python`, `pkill -f <pattern in its own argv>`) instead of by the PID it recorded at start; every matching process on the machine dies - another agent's test run, the owner's live server, or the agent's own shell. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| rate-gate-on-success-path-only | A per-connection rate limit applied to the normal outbound message but not to the other messages the same loop can send (error replies, refusals, retried re-subscriptions): when the normal path fails on every iteration, the loop sends at its poll rate instead of the limit, flooding the client and the shared feed, and the normal answer never arrives. Wider shape: a limit enforced at one send site instead of at the one place every message leaves through is a limit on that site only. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| redirect-bare-path-lands-on-callback-host | A backend redirect to a frontend page written as a bare path ('/broker/connected') resolves against the host the request came in on; when a third party (an OAuth provider) calls the API's own host directly, the browser lands on the API, which serves no pages, so every success and refusal shows a 404 - and tests that assert the bare Location string, or open the page directly, confirm the bug instead of catching it. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| remote-shell-read-transcodes-file | Reading a file through a remote shell command (ssh host 'type file', 'cat' in a PowerShell default shell, Get-Content) returns the shell's re-encoded text, not the file's bytes - the byte-order mark is dropped, line endings are converted and non-ASCII characters are replaced by the console code page; editing that text and writing it back silently rewrites every such line. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| repo-wide-scan-outside-targeted-tests | A repo-wide scan test (one that inspects every module's source, not the module under test) fails on new code that its author never ran it against, because local runs are targeted at the changed area and the scan lives in another folder; the failure surfaces only in CI, one round later, every time a new module is added. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| report-time-typed-not-read | An orchestrator writes clock times into status reports, review logs, briefs or handovers from memory or as an estimate of when something will happen, instead of reading the clock or a commit; the written times drift minutes to hours from reality, including into the future, and the measured expected-vs-actual numbers built on them are wrong. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| request-clock-for-database-stamped-fact | A route writes, or compares against, a fact the DATABASE clock stamps (a grant's granted_at, an instrument load's last_seen_at, an audit event's time) using the request's own clock instead of the database's. In production the two agree, so the defect is invisible; whenever the request clock is pinned, replayed or skewed it refuses valid facts (a fresh grant reads 'not yet active', a fresh load reads 'stale') or the database refuses the write (ADR-023: more than 60 s off its clock). | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| research-finding-held-in-chat | Any research finding proven during a session but reported only in chat (or held back until a decision) is lost to the next reader and lets work proceed on assumptions the finding contradicts; findings must be written to the spec findings list, the spec sections they bear on and (for failure classes) the registry in the same turn they are proven, before any decision or implementation. | unguarded | scope, spec_ref |
| resolution-on-stale-broker-copy | Any manual resolution or state change whose premise (what the broker holds) is read from a stored copy rather than from the latest reconciliation, or any multi-strategy recording that mutates some records before validating all of them, lets the platform act on a broker picture that is no longer true or leave a half-recorded run. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| route-tests-always-override-the-real-reader | A route reads its data through an injected dependency (a reader, loader or store), and every test of that route replaces the dependency with a fake; the real implementation the product calls is never run by any test, so a defect inside it (a wrong argument, a wrong field, a swallowed error) leaves every route test green while every real request fails. Wider shape: any seam that exists for testability becomes a blind spot when no test crosses it with the real thing on the other side. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| row-ahead-dispatched-without-overlap-gate | A builder for a younger row is dispatched into its own worktree without running the binding overlap gate (ADR-171 rule 3) against every older open row, so two rows in flight edit the same file and the older row's fix round collides with the younger row's work. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| rule-over-tables-as-typed-list | A rule that must hold for every table holding a kind of data (every table that stores a strategy definition, every table with a money column) is written as a hand-typed list of table names; a table added by an earlier or later migration is silently left out, and the rule's own test only exercises the tables it names. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| sealed-object-mutable-after-seal | A guard that checks an object when it is BUILT (a seal, a mint token, a type check at construction) but not when it is USED lets any holder change the object in between; every check on the build path passes while the used object carries something the guard never saw. Checking 'is it the sealed type' at the use site has the same hole. Fixing one mutable part (the body) and not its siblings (header names but not values, status) leaves the same class open. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| secret-filter-by-key-name | Any guard that decides whether stored data holds a secret by matching field NAMES against a list (substrings or whole words) both blocks legitimate required fields and lets real secrets through, because no name list is complete for an external API's field names. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| setting-read-from-two-sources | A setting that the settings loader reads from several sources (process environment, a .env file, defaults) but that some code reads directly from one source (os.environ) with its own default gives two answers for the same deployment. A safety switch read that way fails OPEN whenever the value lives only in the other source or is unset and the local default is the permissive one. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| shared-callback-treats-every-return-as-login | When a third party sends the browser back to ONE registered redirect URL for more than one flow (login, and a later action such as placing an order basket), a callback written for the first flow treats every arrival as that flow: a return from the other flow fails the first flow's checks (no state we issued) and the user sees that flow's error - here a login error right after placing real orders - or, if a check happens to pass, the handler runs the first flow's side effects (token exchange, session replace) on the wrong event. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| shared-inflight-marker-without-owner | A machine-wide 'work in flight' marker that records no owner makes every session on the machine obey every other session's marker: one session's long-running check blocks another session's unrelated writes, and no session can tell a live marker of its own from a peer's or a stale one. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| shared-test-db-holds-undeletable-committed-rows | A local run that COMMITS rows into an append-only table of the shared test database (a table whose guard refuses DELETE by design) leaves that database permanently unable to run every test that starts from an empty table, so those tests can no longer be judged on the developer PC and only CI's fresh database can prove them. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| staleness-by-last-change-age | Any data-health rule that calls an instrument stale because its last tick or exchange timestamp is older than a fixed age misflags every quiet but current instrument on a feed that sends only changes, so a healthy chain shows a share of its contracts as stale at all times. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| state-read-after-await | An async UI handler that reads or resets shared reactive state AFTER an await (or an early-return path that does not invalidate in-flight requests) lets a late reply overwrite what the user did meanwhile. Unit tests that settle every promise before the next action (flushPromises) can never see it; a real browser or an e2e that acts while the request is in flight sees it intermittently, so it looks like a flaky test. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| state-with-no-working-exit | Any non-terminal state of a lifecycle (strategy, order, proposal) from which every action the system offers is refused leaves the user stuck with no path forward except acting outside the platform; the explanation shown for that state then points at actions that do not work. A transition table checked only pair-by-pair (is each allowed move allowed?) cannot see this: it needs a reachability check that every reachable non-terminal state has at least one action that succeeds. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| static-guard-scoped-by-name-text | A static repo guard that decides WHICH code it checks by whether the source text contains the target's name (a URL fragment, a helper's identifier, a file-level keyword) misses every case that reaches the same target without spelling the name: a glob or regex pattern that matches it, a helper imported from another file that does the work, an alias, or a second call site in a file that already passed once (per-file instead of per-site checks). | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| store-filled-only-by-tests | A store whose only writers are test fixtures: the write path (guards, revisions, history) is built and verified, and readers are built and verified against fixture rows, but no runnable job or command ever fills the store in a real environment, so every feature reading it is empty outside tests while each piece reports done. Wider shape: a consumer verified before its producer exists looks finished until the first real run. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| store-rule-enforced-per-call-site | A rule about what a store may hold (which source may sit where, which rank wins, which day is frozen) written separately in each write method or caller instead of in one private writer every write passes through; each fix closes the method a test happened to probe, and any other or future write method (or a second store implementation behind the same interface) bypasses it. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| stored-contract-priced-by-reused-token | Any code that turns a STORED contract id into a live price through its exchange feed key (segment:token) without checking that the contract is still live and still holds that token prices the wrong instrument once the exchange reuses the token for a new contract after expiry or delisting. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| sync-check-strict-both-ways | A check that keeps a hand-written list in sync with an external system and fails in BOTH directions (item missing from the list, list naming an item the system no longer has) breaks every open change the moment any change closes an item, until someone edits the list; the break lands on unrelated work. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| targeted-tests-miss-dependent-files | When local runs are limited to the test files a change is 'about' (to save a shared host's CPU), a test in another file that pins the changed behaviour - a status code, a redirect, a message code, a route shape - is skipped, so the change looks green locally and the first full run in CI fails; the selection must be driven by a search for every changed route, code and message across both test trees, not by file names. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| test-asserts-implementation-output | Any test whose expected value was produced by running the code under test (instead of taken from the spec or an independent computation) passes whatever the code does, so a defect in the code is locked in as the 'correct' answer and the suite stays green. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| test-double-encodes-old-assumption | A test double (a stand-in model, a fake server, a socket fake) is written from the builder's assumption of the real thing - an older protocol, a different base class - so tests pass against the double while the real thing fails, or tests fail against the double while the real thing works; the double is not checked against the real implementation it imitates. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| test-skipped-in-its-only-ci-job | A CI fix that makes a red job green with a skip-if-missing (importorskip, skipif on a package or env var) silently drops the test from CI whenever the job that skips it is the only job whose test paths include the file; the job turns green with the tests unrun, and nothing reports that the file now runs nowhere. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| tests-required-names-missing-file | A work item's tests_required can keep naming a test file that a later round deleted or renamed, and no lint or trace check notices, so an acceptance criterion's evidence points at a file that no longer exists while the test that really carries it is unlisted. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| transcript-usage-counted-per-line | A script that sums token usage from a Claude Code transcript (.jsonl) line by line over-counts, because the transcript writes one line per content block of the same assistant message and every such line repeats the message's full usage; any per-line total (tokens, turns) is inflated by the blocks-per-message ratio, while a per-line average stays roughly right, which hides the error. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| trust-broker-status-word | Any handling of broker/execution results that decides the outcome from the latest message (its status word, or the last reported position) instead of an invariant over the whole sequence can hide or clear a position mismatch, letting a new edit or execution start on an unreconciled position. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| verified-on-a-module-the-product-does-not-call | A requirement is marked Verified on evidence about a domain module, and a later product path (a new route, a new integration) re-implements a smaller version of the same behaviour instead of calling that module; the requirement stays Verified while what users reach no longer meets it. Any evidence that names a test file but not the user-facing path that must call the tested code can go stale this way, silently. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| verifier-guard-watches-every-worktree | A write guard that protects a verifier's independence by moving any new file under work/, spec/ or evidence/ while a verifier runs cannot tell the orchestrator's writes from the verifier's, and it watches every worktree of the repo, not only the verifier's own folder - so the orchestrator's cards and spec edits made in parallel, even in a separate worktree, silently disappear into quarantine. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| verifier-writes-outside-sandbox | Any agent whose role is read-only but which can run a shell can write files outside its sandbox; a role boundary stated only in the agent's prompt is not enforced, so its output (here evidence files marked pass/fail with verified_by set by itself) can land in the main checkout and be committed as if the orchestrator had recorded it. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| wall-clock-assertion-flakes-under-load | Any test that asserts elapsed wall-clock time against a fixed threshold (time.perf_counter() - start < N) measures the machine's load, not the code's cost; it fails whenever other work shares the CPU (parallel agents, CI neighbours) and passes on re-run, so a red run carries no information and trains readers to ignore reds. | guarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
| worktree-link-into-main-checkout | Any scratch or review checkout that links (Windows junction or symlink) a folder of the main checkout - typically node_modules to skip an install - turns every later recursive delete of that checkout into a delete of the main checkout's folder: a forced worktree removal, rm -rf or Remove-Item -Recurse walks into the link. The damage is silent (tracked files are unchanged, so git status stays clean) and shows up later as missing packages. | unguarded | occurrences, scope, spec_ref |
